titre_video: How Are Americans Affording $500,000 Homes on Average Salaries?
titre: Reverse housing crisis: cautious lenders and chronic under-building
resume: Advisors recommend spending under a third of gross income on housing, but taxes, insurance and mortgage payments push many toward half. Post-2008 caution shut regular buyers out of lending, while the US has under-built for over a decade and has a deficit of millions of homes. Labor shortages, zoning, land-use rules and land costs paralyzed developers and costs were passed to consumers.
texte: Financial advisors recommend keeping the percentage of gross income spent on housing under a third. But between property taxes, insurance, and mortgage payments, it’s common for it to creep up towards half of available money. This sparked a bizarre reverse housing crisis. The scars of 2008 made traditional lenders so cautious, they shut regular buyers out of the market. Compounding the disaster, the U.S. has been chronically under-building houses for over a decade. The country now has a deficit of millions of homes. Labor shortages, onerous zoning and land-use regulations, and the cost of land has paralyzed developers. And the cost was passed on to consumers.
